chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghayath, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him):

That two men disputed with him regarding a beast of burden, and each of them presented evidence that he had impregnated it, so he ruled in its favor for the one who had it in his possession, and he said: 'If it were not in his possession, I would have divided it between them into two halves.'
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic jurisprudence resolve a dispute over an animal when both parties present equal evidence of ownership?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-yad* (possession) as the primary evidence in civil disputes when competing claims are equally strong, a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for resolving ownership conflicts. This ruling underscores the practical necessity of physical control (*qabd*) as a legal presumption of title, ensuring stability in commercial transactions and property rights within the community.
